Project Preview Description: The Union County initiative bridges the skills gap and drives socioeconomic change by investing in planning, infrastructure, and partnerships.
Project Description: The Union County initiative channels philanthropy into bridging the skills gap by strengthening the local pipeline from classrooms to careers. By investing in planning, infrastructure, and partnerships with institutions across county lines, this work aims to drive long-term socioeconomic change rooted in community leadership.
Key Highlight: The BlackRock Foundation chose to invest not just in programs, but in the infrastructure and vision of the community itself. By equipping local organizations with the capacity and resources for planning, they catalyzed the conditions for resilience and generational impact far beyond the grant window.
Focus Areas: Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Industry, Cradle to Career
Partners: BlackRock Foundation, Partners for Rural Impact, MycoWorks, Union County Schools, Spartanburg County Foundation, United Way of the Piedmont, Spartanburg Academic Movement

Project Preview Description: GKFF takes a neighborhood approach; listening, mapping, and tailoring strategies to build trust, capacity, and reflect Tulsa’s diverse communities.
Project Description: George Kaiser Family Foundation (GKFF) works neighborhood by neighborhood, listening to residents and mapping assets to meet specific needs. By tailoring strategies to zip codes, GKFF builds trust, strengthens community capacity, and ensures initiatives like cultural hubs and incubators celebrate lived experiences of Tulsa's diverse neighborhoods.
Key Highlight: GKFF takes a fundamentally different approach to philanthropy by committing to generations rather than grant cycles. Its investments are designed to address systemic barriers that create durable pathways to upward mobility. By tackling interlocking issues that range from education and workforce to build environment, and paired with a neighborhood-by-neighborhood strategy, GKFF centers their work around the goal of handing over the keys to residents so that communities themselves can lead and sustain lasting change.
Focus Areas: Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Housing, Community Leadership, Skills Training, Arts & Culture, Public Space
Partners: George Kaiser Family Foundation, Eastside Rise, Northside Neighbors, Growing Together Tulsa

Project Preview Description: SOAR’s EKY Runway Program helps Eastern Kentuckians overcome employment barriers, find purpose, and build lasting careers through a whole-human approach.
Project Description: SOAR’s EKY Runway Program helps Eastern Kentuckians overcome barriers to employment and discover purpose and dignity through meaningful work. By implementing a "whole human" approach, the program opens pathways to lasting careers.
Key Highlight: In its first year of existence, the EKY Runway has reengaged more than 80 individuals previously outside the workforce and navigated them back into employment. This has generated more than $2.5 million in new wages. The program is proving that with, the right supports, disadvantaged populations can return to work, find purpose through meaningful employment, and escape generational poverty.
Focus Areas: Skills Training, Economic Opportunity, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding
Partners: Microsoft TechSpark, EKY Runway Program & SOAR, Volunteers of America Mid-States, Appalachian Regional Healthcare, Pikeville Medical Center, Commonwealth of Kentucky, U.S. Economic Development Administration

Project Name: Annie E. Casey Foundation & South Atlanta
Project Preview Description: South Atlanta’s long-term transformation blends community-led investment, generational support, and civic infrastructure to build resilient families.
Project Description: South Atlanta is transforming through long-term investment and community leadership. For 20+ years a two-generation approach has strengthened children’s development and parents’ economic stability. Civic projects, like Pittsburgh Yards, boost entrepreneurship and community spaces, with residents leading, engaging, and shaping sustainable change.
Key Highlight: The Annie E. Casey Foundation advances a two-generation place-based strategy in South Atlanta supporting children’s development and parents’ economic stability while investing in civic infrastructure through Pittsburgh Yards. This 31-acre redevelopment features the Nia Building, maker spaces, community greenspace, and pad-ready sites, all co-designed with residents and in support of the community. The new Container Courtyard of storefronts and studios adds new energy along the Atlanta BeltLine’s Southside Trail and showcases the creativity of local entrepreneurs.
Focus Areas: Cradle to Career, Economic Opportunity, Retail, Industry, Public Space, Arts & Culture, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Community Leadership
Partners: Annie E. Casey Foundation, Pittsburgh Yards

Project Preview Description: City of Homes turns vacant properties into affordable homes, tackling inequities and revitalizing disinvested neighborhoods.
Project Description: City of Homes is an affordable housing initiative redeveloping vacant and blighted properties into affordable homes. Supported by cross-sector partners, the program’s supporters adjusted the attorney receivership model, enabling nonprofit property acquisitions, addressing inequities in homeownership and stabilizing long-disinvested neighborhoods.
Key Highlight: City of Homes introduces a new tool in the affordable housing landscape by blending philanthropy, public investment, local government support, and legal innovation. Not only does the initiative expand access to homeownership for communities of color historically shut out of the market, it also demonstrates how redevelopment of vacant properties can create generational wealth and build long-term neighborhood stability. Recognition through the 2024 Massachusetts Bond Bill and the Gateway Cities Innovator Award underscores City of Homes’ potential as a replicable model.
Focus Areas: Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Housing
Partners: MassMutual Foundation, Way Finders

Project Preview Description: Union Capital proves that investing in social capital can transform communities, rewarding civic engagement and connecting residents to vital resources.
Project Description: Union Capital redefines community building by showing that investing in social capital can be as transformative as investing in physical infrastructure. By providing invitations, incentives, and connections to information, one can overcome barriers to engaging with their community and access critical resources for prosperity.
Key Highlight: Union Capital’s model builds power by valuing and rewarding the everyday ways residents already strengthen their communities. By converting civic participation into tangible recognition and resources, it transforms social connections into a durable form of capital. This approach makes social networks a lever for resilience and mobility, and it stands out as a distinctive strategy in the community development landscape. The program's expansion into Springfield, positions Springfield as a model for how targeted philanthropy can help fuel long-term community resilience and economic mobility.
Focus Areas: Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Community Leadership
Partners: MassMutual Foundation

Project Preview Description: BMC’s Economic Justice Hub boosts Boston families’ financial health through coaching, benefits support, job pathways, and research on benefit cliffs.
Project Description: The Economic Justice Hub at Boston Medical Center (BMC) strengthens the financial health of families in Boston who are served through its pediatric care system. Building on the success of BMC’s StreetCred program, the Hub provides financial coaching, benefits navigation, and job pathway support.
Key Highlight: The Economic Justice Hub shows how wealth and health are deeply intertwined, with economic inequities at the root of many health disparities. By embedding financial resources, workforce pathways, and policy research into clinical care, Boston Medical Center is addressing the structural drivers of poor health outcomes and advancing a place-based model that connects economic mobility and healthcare. It also advances policy research focused on the cliff effect, which is the sudden loss of public benefits that can occur when household income increases.
Focus Areas: Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Economic Opportunity
Partners: MassMutual Foundation, Boston Medical Center

Project Preview Description: NeighborShare connects donors to verified local needs; its Springfield pilot delivers fast, transparent aid for everyday emergencies.
Project Description: NeighborShare is a direct-giving platform connecting donors to neighbors with identified needs, and validated by trusted nonprofits across the country. This model provides fast, transparent support for those facing emergencies like childcare, medical bills, or car repairs, preventing small setbacks from becoming larger crises.
Key Highlight: What makes NeighborShare unique is its ability to transform micro-level giving into systemic resilience. By pairing immediacy and transparency with nonprofit validation, it turns one-time acts of generosity into a trusted safety net that strengthens both households and the community as a whole. Building on lessons from Springfield, the MassMutual Foundation supported NeighborShare’s expansion to Boston, embedding the peer-to-peer giving approach more broadly across the state.
Focus Areas: Community Leadership, Care Support Systems
Partners: MassMutual Foundation, NeighborShare

Project Preview Description: The Delta Philanthropy Forum unites cross-sector stakeholders to addresses poverty in the Delta Region through collaboration and community voice.
Project Description: The Delta Philanthropy Forum (DPF) unites philanthropies, CDFIs, and investors to address persistent poverty in the Arkansas–Mississippi Delta by pooling resources and elevating community voices.
Key Highlight: The Delta Philanthropy Forum has raised awareness of the region’s severe underfunding, built cross-sector coalitions on capacity building, education and economic mobility. Through convenings that amplify emerging leaders and community-driven strategies, DPF is working with the community to shift the Delta to a more coordinated and opportunity-focused region.
Focus Areas: Economic Opportunity, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding
Partners: Arkansas Impact Philanthropy, Arkansas Community foundation, Carl B. & Florence E. King Foundation, University of Arkansas, Community Foundation of Northwest Mississippi, Washington County Economic Alliance, Derek Lewis Foundation, Foundation for the Mid South, Mississippi Alliance of Nonprofits and Philanthropy, Walton Family Foundation, Winthrop Rockefeller Foundation, WKKF, WHEF, Clinton School Center of Community Philanthropy, Philanthropy Southeast

Project Preview Description: KPMG is investing $1M over three years in Orlando’s 32805 area code, partnering with local groups to advance community well-being.
Project Description: KPMG is investing over $1 million over three years in the 32805 neighborhoods, partnering with the AdventHealth for Children Foundation, Lift Orlando, United Against Poverty and other community collaborators to build a comprehensive, place-based approach to community well-being.
Key Highlight: Funding has supported a full-time pediatric mental health counselor at the AdventHealth Early Learning Center and a full-time program manager for Lift Orlando's EmpowerEd Scholars program. The partnership has activated a range of programs, including training at daycare centers, and strengthening learning ecosystems through art and motion therapy workshops for educators delivered in partnership with United Arts of Central Florida. KPMG’s support has extended to Lift Orlando’s EmpowerEd Scholars Program, providing resources such as financial aid nights and dorm showers. Together, these efforts show how corporate partners can weave healthcare, education, and cultural assets into a neighborhood strategy.
Focus Areas: Skills Training, Economic Opportunity, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Cradle to Career, Arts & Culture
Partners: LIFT Orlando, Advent Health West Lakes Early Learning Center, United Arts of Central Florida, United Against Poverty, AdventHealth Foundation

Project Preview Description: MPN functions as both a network convener, resource, and a collaborative architect, enabling funders to come together, learn together, and act together.
Project Description: MPN functions as both a network convener, resource, and a collaborative architect, enabling funders to come together, learn together, and act together.
Key Highlight: Instead of acting singularly, philanthropic infrastructure organizations serve as the central convener and coordinator for funders — aligning strategies, pooling resources, and driving a collective shift from giving in the short-term to long-term systemic change and equity. This structure enables funders to co-design with communities, share risk, and adapt together, creating a more powerful and systemic approach to tackling issues alongside grantees and the broader community.
Focus Areas: Housing, Arts & Culture, Community Leadership, Economic Opportunity
Partners: Maryland Philanthropy Network

Project Preview Description: Play Equity Fund, a trusted intermediary, strengthens neighborhood organizations so every young person has access to recreation and safe spaces to play.
Project Description: In Los Angeles, philanthropy is advancing play equity; the idea that every young person, deserves access to sports, recreation, and safe spaces to play. Rather than building new infrastructure, funders channel resources through the Play Equity Fund, a trusted intermediary that strengthens existing neighborhood organizations. This approach reweaves a fragmented system into a cohesive movement, amplifying small, hyper-local groups and ensuring that investments reflect community priorities across one of the nation’s most diverse and sprawling cities.
Key Highlight: By partnering with organizations, like the Play Equity Fund, to strengthen sports-based youth development and reimagine the built environment, LA’s play equity movement is making life-changing moments more common, accessible, and equitable across neighborhoods.
Focus Areas: Sports, Community Leadership, Care Support Systems, Public Space, Youth Leadership
Partners: LA84 Foundation, The Social Justice Learning Institute, Nike Foundation, Play Equity Fund, Youth N Motion Academy

Project Preview Description: As part of Cisco’s 40 Communities initiative, the work in Western North Carolina focuses on long-term recovery and community resilience.
Project Description: As part of their 40 Communities initiative, Cisco supports housing recovery efforts, contributing to the repair of 220+ homes and supporting partners in expanding their work. Cisco works with local organizations to advance community resilience hubs, enabling communication and access to critical services; helping communities recover while building a stronger, more resilient foundation for the future.
Key Highlight: This initiative brings together immediate, tangible recovery, helping families return to safe housing, with longer-term investments in connectivity and communications resilience, creating a coordinated and scalable approach to how communities prepare for and respond to challenges.
Focus Areas: Housing, Public Space, Economic Opportunity, Skills Training, Community Leadership
Partners: Cisco

Project Preview Description: LISC has made a multi-year, multi-million dollar commitment to South Everett, serving as the lead convener of a cross-sector initiative to implement an ambitious economic agenda.
Project Description: LISC has made a multi-year, multi-million dollar commitment to South Everett, serving as the lead convener of a cross-sector initiative to implement an ambitious economic agenda. Implementation is now underway and involves implementing an affordable housing strategy, expanding workforce development programs, capacity building for community organizations, and more.
Key Highlight: This effort is particularly impactful based on the deep relationships between partners, long-term commitment to moving at the speed of trust, and the way that community is centered in the work.
Focus Areas: Arts & Culture, Economic Opportunity, Public Space, Community Leadership, Retail, Housing, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding
Partners: Housing Consortium of Everett and Snohomish County, City of Everett, StationsUnidos, Connect Casino Road, LISC Puget Sound

Project Preview Description: Project Petals is dedicated to transforming underresourced, frontline and BIPOC communities through environmental advocacy, revitalization, training and food security.
Project Description: Project Petals is dedicated to transforming underresourced, frontline and BIPOC communities through environmental advocacy, green space revitalization, leadership training and food security. Project Petals works with communities to build and maintain green spaces while identifying and empowering the next generation of climate leaders.
Key Highlight: Founded by Alicia White in 2015, Project Petals has grown from a local Queens effort into a globally recognized, United Nations Environmental Programme-accredited organization. The organization now supports hundreds of climate and environmental leaders from frontline communities across New York City and gives thousands of people access to gardens, urban farms, and community green spaces.
Focus Areas: Youth Leadership, Criminal Justice, Social Justice, Public Space
Partners: United Nations Environmental Programme, Vital Voices, Project Petals

Project Preview Description: Project OneTen provides programming for boys of color during the critical transition to high school.
Project Description: Project OneTen provides programming for boys of color during the critical transition to high school. Through coaching, community building, and research-based curriculum, they create spaces for boys to cultivate their strengths and unique identities to build a foundation for success in high school and beyond.
Key Highlight: The organization supports high-potential referred students who live or attend a Chicago Public School on the city's South or West sides, where the outcome disparities are greatest. The support offered by this program extends beyond academic support; students are guided through a yearlong educator-advised curriculum designed to promote leadership skills, community-building and self-awareness.  In just 4 years of full-time operation, the organization has grown to support over 1000+ students through a mix of in-school and out-of-school programming.
Focus Areas: Youth Leadership
Partners: Project OneTen, A Better Chicago, New Schools Venture Fund, Chicago Scholars, Obama Foundation's MBK Initiative, Chicago Public Schools

Project Preview Description: WilmingtoNColor Heritage Tours is a public history and cultural tourism initiative, designed to preserve and share historically overlooked African American narratives.
Project Description: WilmingtoNColor reconnects communities to place, restores suppressed narratives, and uses heritage tourism as a tool for education, economic development, and cultural preservation. By bringing thousands of visitors into direct engagement with local history, they reshape public understanding while creating economic opportunities for local businesses and communities.
Key Highlight: WilmingtoNColor is one of the only experiences in the country that combines immersive, audiovisual storytelling with live, place-based historical interpretation centered on a suppressed American event like the 1898 Wilmington coup. The program educates thousands annually, partners with local institutions, and drives economic activity to Black-owned and community-rooted businesses. What makes this initiative unique is its ability to function as both a mobile museum and economic driver, transforming tourism into a tool for truth-telling, reconciliation, and community reinvestment.
Focus Areas: Youth Leadership, Social Justice, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Economic Opportunity, Arts & Culture, Community Leadership
Partners: WilmingtoNColor Heritage Tours

Project Name: The Clark on 54th Community Benefits Fund
Project Preview Description: Clark on 54th Community Benefits Fund is a mixed-income, multi-family development at Crenshaw and 54th St in South LA - a corridor shaped by redlining and displacement.
Project Description: The Clark on 54th Community Benefits Fund is a mixed-income, multi-family housing development located at Crenshaw and 54th St in South LA - a corridor shaped by decades of redlining, disinvestment, & accelerating displacement. Their mission is to deliver long-term affordable housing, build community wealth, and establish a replicable model for locally rooted, equity-driven neighborhood revitalization.
Key Highlight:
Slated for completion in December 2026, the development will deliver 48 units, with 21% designated as affordable at Very Low Income AMI levels. These units' affordability is sustained through philanthropic and impact investment, making community partnerships essential to their viability.

The development includes dedicated space for Black retail owners, public art, and outdoor space, ensuring that existing residents and communities benefit from neighborhood change.

The Clark on 54th is proof that communities can lead their own revitalization - and that affordable housing can be delivered without reliance on traditional government subsidy when the right partnerships are in place.
Focus Areas: Housing
Partners: Regenaissance, Praxis Development Group, LISC LA

Project Preview Description: A 10-year, place-based strategy to transform East Harris County; where every resident has a clear pathway to opportunity, economic mobility, and long-term stability.
Project Description: The East Harris County Empowerment Council (EHCEC) serves as the region’s development anchor, aligning public, private, and philanthropic partners around a shared vision for inclusive growth. Through this Blueprint, EHCEC is stewarding and influencing more than $100 million in coordinated investments to drive lasting, systems-level change.
Key Highlight: The strategy is built on five priorities that work together to reshape the region: strengthening community resilience, expanding economic opportunity pathways, growing local leadership, building organizational capacity, and aligning systems through a unified regional approach. Rather than operating disconnected programs, the Blueprint creates a coordinated system of opportunity that connects residents to education, careers, resources, and leadership while aligning institutions and funding toward shared outcomes. This work positions East Harris County as a model for how regions can organize, align capital, and execute long-term transformation at scale.
Focus Areas: Economic Opportunity, Economic Mobility & Generational Wealthbuilding, Community Leadership
Partners: East Harris County Empowerment Council

Project Preview Description: The Appalachian Cradle to Career Partnership (APPC2C) is a place-based initiative working to create brighter futures in Appalachian Kentucky.
Project Description: The Appalachian Cradle to Career Partnership (APPC2C) is a place-based initiative working to create brighter futures in Appalachian Kentucky. We partner with schools, libraries, and local organizations to align around four strategic priorities: reducing chronic absenteeism, strengthening youth mental health, expanding access to paid work experiences and improving early childhood education.
Key Highlight: Local school district policies were shifted to allow the school district to act as a local workforce partner for the Appalachian Promise Learn and Earn Internship Program, which offers 16 hours of learning and 32 hours of earning per week, including hybrid and fully remote options. The policy change was needed to align with businesses that wanted interns to work remotely and contributed to our success in placing 300 interns across eight counties. Participants benefited from exposure to career options not found in their community and gained workforce experience while earning wages.
Focus Areas: Cradle to Career
Partners: Partners for Rural Impact, Strive Together
